national_raw_news.title: Home Minister Amit Shah meets family members of anti-drugs activists in Punjab
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah met the family members of Vikramjit Singh in Batala, Gurdaspur, in Punjab, today. Vikramjit Singh was allegedly killed by drug traffickers recently. The Home Minister is on a day-long visit to Punjab to meet the family members of those who paid with their lives in Mansa, Gurdaspur and Sangrur recently for raising their voices against drug menace in the state. Mr Amit Shah will also meet the family members of Gulzar Singh in Sangrur, who committed suicide allegedly when his pleas were not heard by the state government against the sale of drugs, which made his son a drug addict. He will also visit Mansa, where an anti-drug activist, Parvinder Singh Jhota, was recently shot dead by a chemist for objecting to selling synthetic drugs. The Home Minister will meet his bereaved family members. The body of the activist has not been cremated by his family even after a week of his murder. Jhota’s father, Bhim Singh, an ex-serviceman, while welcoming the visit, has demanded a CBI probe in the case. Meanwhile, Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann has declared to hand over the murder case of Parvinder Singh to Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). Later, Sh. Shah will participate in Dussehra ceremony at Ludhiana, where the burning of Ravana’s effigy has symbolically been themed as ‘Ravan of Chitta.’

national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) must convert the political vision of its leaders into practical cooperation that is visible in the lives of the people of the region. Addressing the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in Tajikistan today, Mr Singh said that the organisation’s 25-year journey provided an opportunity to review its achievements and discuss its future direction. The Minister emphasised that the three pillars of security, connectivity and opportunity are mutually reinforcing and essential for achieving tangible benefits for the people. Mr Singh said terrorism remains one of the gravest threats to peace and development of the region. He said that terrorism causes the loss of innocent lives, disrupts investment and economic capabilities, radicalises societies and deprives young people of opportunities. Mr Singh asserted that there can be no justification for terrorism, no double standards in combating it, and no place for those who finance, support or provide safe havens to terrorists. He called for collectively dismantling the entire ecosystem of terrorism. The Minister said that India supports initiatives that link markets, facilitate trade and create new development opportunities. He said that the International North-South Transport Corridor and Chabahar Port could significantly contribute to connecting Central Asia with wider markets. Mr Singh stressed that connectivity projects must be based on consultation and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the countries. Mr Singh also highlighted India’s experience in harnessing technology and innovation for development. He said India’s Digital Public Infrastructure has transformed public service delivery and expanded financial inclusion, while the country has built one of the world’s largest startup ecosystems. The Minister also said that India will host the first SCO Civilisation Dialogue Forum later this year and invited all SCO member states to participate.

national_raw_news.title: Home Minister Amit Shah to Visit Punjab, Meet Families of Anti-Drug Activists Killed in the State 7 hours ago 137
national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah will visit Punjab today to meet with the families of anti-drug activists who recently lost their lives after raising their voices against synthetic drug traffickers in the state. This includes the recent broad daylight murder of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, who was shot dead in broad daylight by a chemist selling synthetic drugs when Jhota publicly opposed him in Mansa recently. Our Jalandhar correspondent reports that the body of the activist has not been cremated by his family even after a week of his murder. His father has said he will not cremate his son till justice is delivered. Jhota’s father, Bhim Singh, an ex-serviceman, while welcoming the visit, has demanded a CBI probe in the case. Meanwhile, Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) leader and former Member of Parliament Harsimrat Kaur Badal, in a letter to the Union Home Minister, has requested to order an independent CBI probe into Jhota’s murder and the wider drug trade in the state. She has demanded an exemplary punishment for those responsible for silencing voices against drugs in Punjab. Mr Shah will also be meeting the family members of those who were allegedly killed in Gurdaspur by drug traffickers and the one, a father of a substance user, who committed suicide in Sangrur district. Later, the Home Minister is also scheduled to attend the Dussehra ceremonies in Ludhiana. Rajesh Bali/Jalandhar/Mail/0730

national_raw_news.title: Living Museum at Mizo Typical Village in Falkawn Draws Visitors, Promotes Mizo Culture and Traditions 3 hours ago 40
national_raw_news.content: The Living Museum at Zokhua, the Mizo Typical Village in Falkawn, is attracting considerable interest by offering visitors a chance to experience traditional Mizo customs and ways of life first-hand. Since opening, the museum has welcomed a steady stream of visitors. Set up by the Art and Culture Department, the Mizo Typical Village aims to give younger generations a practical insight into the lives and traditions of their ancestors. It also serves as an educational resource for schoolchildren, helping them better understand topics covered in their textbooks. Visitors can explore and buy locally made Mizo handicrafts, while the initiative also provides a source of income for local residents and young people. The Living Museum, which offers visitors a closer look at Mizo culture, holds live demonstrations every Saturday for an entry fee of Rs 100. These include demonstrations of traditional practices, along with cultural entertainment featuring folk music and dance. Officials of the Art and Culture Department said the initiative was introduced in response to the growing number of visitors from outside Mizoram and increasing interest in local tourism among residents. They said the museum was intended to offer visitors more opportunities to experience Mizo culture firsthand while helping preserve and promote traditional customs and practices. The museum has been attracting a large number of visitors, they added. Activities at the Living Museum include demonstrations of traditional village life, traditional dances, folk songs and dances, indigenous games, traditional Mizo cuisine and traditional costumes.
